topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets the stage for the lecture by contextualizing complement within immunology and addressing its complexity.

topics.label: Foundations of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overarching principles, terminology, and central role of component C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream biochemical pathways that trigger complement activation and converge on the threshold of C3 convertase formation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream biological actions through which activated complement eliminates pathogens and drives inflammatory clearance.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical presentations and disease susceptibilities resulting from genetic or acquired defects in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the evolutionary mechanisms employed by pathogens, exemplified by Staphylococcus aureus, to circumvent complement-mediated clearance.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks for the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
